summary: The SwiftUI shell: the sky and theme, components, navigation, sign-in, the agreement, legal pages, accounts and settings.

src/App.jsx.note: The app's states (the legal pages, restoring, a sign-in that came back without a session, the agreement screen and its checking line, the front page, the shell, remade per account), useProfile, and the archive's provider (ArchiveHost, one ArchiveModel per signed-in account, its store in the app's file store; deleting an account's data deletes its archive and starts every store handle afresh). Not yet: the composer's provider and a compose link kept from before a sign-in (pendingCompose.js, VirgaPosting's), the dashboards' provider (the shell reads the stored dashboards itself, ShellDashboards.swift), keepScansFor (Defense), and drawing the shell again when the formats change. On iOS a sign-in comes back into the running app, so a failed one is the session's error on whatever page is up.

src/accounts/AccountMenu.jsx.note: All of it, with the compact menu's Sync now once there is an archive to sync. A native Menu: an account's row carries a person glyph, since a native menu item can't show the picture. The pending-work read before a long session's sign-out goes through AppModel.pendingWork, nil until VirgaPosting's schedule and timer services are wired to Virga's server; until then the sign-out says it couldn't check, as the web does when the read fails.

src/accounts/AccountsSettings.jsx.note: All of it; the pending-work warnings read through AppModel.pendingWork, nil until VirgaPosting's schedule and timer services are wired, so a long session reads as one that couldn't be checked. Refocusing the next row's ⋯ after a removal is the system's.

src/accounts/SessionNotices.jsx.note: The hand-off before a sign-in again (with Cancel), the stuck account's button and the sign-in's notices. Deliberately not: 'another tab switched accounts', since every window of the app shares one session (AppModel).

src/accounts/accounts.css.note: The rows of Settings › Account, the front page's remembered accounts and the session notices. The account menu's list styles are the native Menu's on iOS.

src/charts/charts.css.note: The chart tokens (--chart-1/2, --chart-area, --chart-grid, --chart-ghost, --heat-0 to 6, --second-tip), the series chart's strokes, dashes, dots and marks, the tooltip's own grounds, the table view, the bar list, the heatmap and the sparkline. Not as the web: the plot's margins and the rules' numbers are Swift Charts' own layout, and the widget's hidden marks list (.widget .an-chart-marks) waits for the dashboards.

src/components/Delta.jsx.note: DeltaView(pct:title:plain:) draws ChartFormat.deltaText(pct) (charts/format.js, VirgaArchive): nil is "new"; a caller with no comparison at all (the web's undefined) draws none. The title is read by VoiceOver as a hint.

src/legal/TermsGate.jsx.note: All of it but the Reload link after TERMS_VERSION_MISMATCH: the app's documents are bundled, so loading them again can't bring newer ones; the words still say so.

src/pages/Landing.jsx.note: All of it but the live sky and the five taps on the mark (src/hillside), and the compose link's callout (composing), which waits for pendingCompose.js.

src/settings/SettingsPage.jsx.note: The index (a phone's), Account, Data and sync (the archive's line, the sync's steps and Cancel, what failed, Sync now or the rest of a build, Rebuild posts and its dialog, the JSON and CSV exports through the system's exporter, where it is kept with the app folder's size for the web's storage estimate, and Delete this archive with its dialog, the toast and the way home), Appearance (the sky, the accent with its swatches, contrast, density, the sidebar, numbers and dates), Permissions and About (with the Terms and the Privacy Policy, the agreement's date, and when the repo was last read). Not yet: Dashboards (their editing) and Posting (the posting settings), each of which shows its header and says it isn't in the app yet; Appearance's live sky (the hillside). Data's "Keep it when space runs low" is shown only where the browser can be asked (navigator.storage.persist), which iOS has no counterpart for, so it isn't drawn.

src/settings/settings.css.note: The index, the section, the row, the permissions and sources lists, the sky's tiles and the accent's choices. The dashboards' list, the sync and the default timer's editor come with their sections.

src/shell/CommandPalette.jsx.note: The palette as a full-height sheet, over VirgaInsights' Commands (buildCommands with CommandContext.app, paletteGroups, rememberRecent and parseRecent under virga:palette-recent, moveActive): the field on its line with Close, the groups, each option's icon (the account's picture for another account), title, hint (under the title on a phone, once there is a search) and tick, the empty line, the foot beside the sidebar, the result count read out, and the arrows, Home, End, Return and Escape on a hardware keyboard. Search in the app bar, the sidebar and the rail opens it, and ⌘K. Running: an address through the navigator, Sync, the period (with the web's toast), the sky, another account; New post goes to the composer's address. Not yet: Customize this dashboard and New dashboard, left out of the list until the dashboards' editing is ported, and the composer itself.

src/shell/FirstRun.jsx.note: The first build's page, word for word: what a build reads and where it goes, the store's warning when the archive would only last the session, Build your archive (a full sync), the steps while it runs (SyncSteps), and what failed. Shown by RoutedPage where a route needs the archive and it isn't built.

src/shell/MobileNav.jsx.note: The tab bar and the app bar: on a part's front page the mark, Search and the account in the page's content, scrolling away with the sky; inside a part the system's back button with the page above's name, Search and the account, in the navigation bar; Search opens the command palette, and the account's menu holds Sync now once there is an archive.

src/shell/Shell.jsx.note: The shell by the window's width (from 900 Virga's own sidebar beside the page, held to --shell-max and centred, with one sky behind both that the page's scroll moves; under it a stack with the app bar and tab bar), the address as its state, every route to a page (a page not ported yet shows its header and says so), NotFound, the dashboard redirect and the last dashboard looked at, the titles, the archive's opening line and the first build's page where a route needs it, and the sync's places (the sidebar's card, or the strip at the top of the page, neither while the first build's page is up). The command palette (from Search, and ⌘K on a hardware keyboard) and the toasts are mounted here. Not yet: New dashboard, the composer and its shortcut (New post goes to the composer's address), and the live sky.

src/shell/Sidebar.jsx.note: The parts as words with the open one's pages, the account, New post, folding to the rail, and the archive's lines at the foot (SyncCard, brief beside the first build's page; on the rail Sync now is in the account's menu). Search or jump to… with its shortcut (a search glyph on the rail) opens the command palette. Not yet: New dashboard, and the mark's five taps (the live sky).

src/shell/SyncStatus.jsx.note: overallFraction, syncHeadline, syncStepText, syncWhen, useArchiveCounts and runFor (SyncStatus), SyncCard at the sidebar's foot, SyncBanner at the top of a phone's page and beside the folded rail (drawn by VirgaPage), and SyncSteps on the first build's page. The steps' names and lines are VirgaArchive's SyncProgress. The role=status lines are read as updating frequently.

src/shell/bits.jsx.note: The mark, the page header, toasts (ToastCenter and ToastStack; nothing pushes one yet), useIsNarrow (the theme's hasSidebar), usePeriod (PreferencesModel.period(), setPeriod, setCustomPeriod over VirgaArchive's Periods), PeriodPicker (the presets and Custom; on a phone Custom is its calendar alone) and RangeDialog (two days on the system's date picker in the active time zone, checked as they are picked, with the web's three problems and its line on what the range covers). Not yet: useSkyTaps (the live sky).

src/shell/commandPalette.css.note: The field (no box, a 2-point rule in ink, 52 tall, --text-lg and 16 from 374 down), Close on its line, the list's groups and options (40 tall, 48 on a phone, the highlighted one on --hover), the tick, the empty line, the foot and the keys (.kbd), a phone's hints under the titles and waiting for a search. The sheet is the system's at every width: the web's dialog near the top of a wide screen (620 wide, 12vh down) has no counterpart.

src/shell/shell.css.note: The shell, its figure size, the sidebar and rail, the page header and body, the app bar and tab bar, dialogs, choices and toasts, the sync's places, the first run, the period picker and the range dialog's fields. The sidebar's search row and the app bar's Search button too. Not yet: the sidebar list's overflow fades.

src/signin/HandleField.jsx.note: All of it but moving through the suggestions with a hardware keyboard's arrows (moveActive): a press picks one.

src/styles/app.css.note: a few of its measures (the landing page's bar, title, lede and points, the return screen's title, the restoring message and its animation) are in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme, from ios/parity/cases/_themeKit.js); it sets no theme tokens. The pages are VirgaUI's: the front page, its hero, points, foot and sketch (Pages/LandingView.swift), the narrow column and the restoring line (Pages/SignInReturnView.swift), with the measures ThemeKit doesn't read named in Theme/Measures.swift until _themeKit.js reads them; the live sky's frame waits for the hillside

src/styles/base.css.note: the page's type (body size, line height, numerals, headings, links, code), focus outline, selection and the sky's wash are measures in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme); it sets no theme tokens. VirgaUI draws them: the type in Instrument Sans with tabular figures (Theme/Typography.swift), the sky from the window's top behind the page, moved by its scroll, and once behind the sidebar and the page together beside the sidebar (Theme/SkyWash.swift), the focus outline (Components/Focus.swift), Reduce Motion (Theme/Motion.swift). The element resets, ::selection and the helper classes (.visually-hidden, .skip-link) have no counterpart on iOS

src/styles/controls.css.note: 246 of its declarations, the kit's measures, are in ThemeKit (VirgaCore/Theme, listed in ios/parity/cases/_themeKit.js). The components are VirgaUI's (Components/): the button's tiers and sizes, the link action and the more link, Segmented and the sideways row, the section and its head, foot and caption, the row and its actions, figures and the delta, the menu (native), fields and the text area, the check and the switch, badges, the meta line, chips, tokens, avatars, the dot, the table, the empty state, the note, the callout, the disclosure, progress, the info tip, and the touch block's sizes. Not yet: the list toolbar (.list-toolbar), the chart foot (.chart-foot) and select.input's own chevron (a native Picker), which come with the pages that use them; a few touch reaches ThemeKit doesn't read are in Theme/Measures.swift

src/styles/theme.css.note: every token it sets on <html> and the cascade that picks them, in VirgaCore/Theme, resolved at a window's root and read as @Environment(\.virgaTheme) (Theme/VirgaTheme.swift). Its high-contrast rules for components are drawn in VirgaUI: the focus outline (Components/Focus.swift), a pressed key's line (Components/Segmented.swift), the switch, its knob at 70% (Components/Switch.swift), the narrow tab bar's disc's ring (Shell/MobileNav.swift); not yet heat cells and bar tracks (the charts), the current page's underline and the image labels. Its forced-colours rules are recorded but never apply: no device the app runs on has them.
